segments.title: HOW TO BUY SHARES
segments.say: Zim stocks, part two of four. Here's exactly how to buy shares in Zimbabwe, step by step. How to actually buy shares. It's easier than most people think.

segments.title: WHAT YOU NEED
segments.note: Requirements as found on C-Trade and SECZiM. Brokers may ask for more.
segments.say: You need three things: your ID, proof of residence, and a Zimbabwean bank account. With those, you open a CSD account. That's the electronic register that records which shares you own. It's run by the Chengetedzai Depository Company, and you open it through a licensed stockbroker or custodian.

segments.title: THREE WAYS TO BUY
segments.note: Platforms as found: ctrade.co.zw, ZSE Direct (ZSE). Minimums per ZSE Direct.

items.sub: buy and sell from your phone
start from a ZiG 50 deposit, ZiG 20 order

segments.say: Then you choose how to buy. One: through a stockbroker. Always check they're registered with SECZiM, the Securities and Exchange Commission. Two: the C-Trade app, which lets you trade from your phone. Three: ZSE Direct. As I found out, you can start there with a deposit of just 50 ZiG, and orders from 20 ZiG.

segments.title: WHAT IT COSTS
segments.note: Fees: SECZiM published transaction-cost table (as found). Check current charges with your broker.

items.text: Capital gains tax on the VFEX

segments.say: And it costs money to trade. Going by SECZiM's published table, buying costs about 1.7 percent, and selling about 2.4 percent, including a 1 percent capital gains withholding tax. So a share has to rise around 4 percent just for you to break even. On the VFEX, there's no capital gains tax.
